Subject: Private catalog commercial onboarding - LumenHealth

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this week — LumenHealth is excited to move forward with a private catalog listing on Azure and to get Redwood set up as the publisher for our internal procurement flow. Procurement has requested a short commercial summary and a PO template so they can start internal approvals (we're targeting a July 1st start).

High level:
- Initial committed spend: $120k USD over 12 months (monthly invoicing preferred)
- Preferred billing entity: LumenHealth, Inc. (EIN on attached PO template)
- Entitlements: 3 publisher seats + API access for dev/test environment
- Compliance: we will require SOC2 evidence and a basic attestation for data handling

Can you: (1) confirm the invoicing path for Azure private catalog purchases (publisher-billed vs. marketplace-billed), (2) provide a commercial summary sheet we can attach to the PO, and (3) indicate any gating items for onboarding (Azure seller auth, publisher onboarding, PO terms you cannot accept)?

I've attached our PO template for your legal team to review: Lumen_PO_template_LumenHealth.pdf (stub).

Thanks,
Evelyn Carter
Head of Procurement
LumenHealth

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the clear summary and the PO template. Looping in Marissa (sales) and Jonas (legal) plus Rishi (finance) to accelerate routing.

Quick answers up front:
1) Invoicing path: for Azure private catalog we support two options — (A) publisher-billed (Redwood invoices LumenHealth directly) or (B) marketplace-billed (Azure invoices and remits to Redwood). Publisher-billed is usually faster for PO routing on your side; marketplace-billed is common for customers that require a single Azure invoice. We can do either.
2) Commercial summary: attached — Redwood_Commercial_Summary_v2.xlsx. It highlights unit pricing, entitlements, and recommended metering configuration for the private catalog SKU.
3) Onboarding gating items: seller authorization (Azure publisher account), billing entity confirmation, and standard DPA + PO terms. SOC2 evidence we can provide — I'll attach the governance checklist and raise any special redlines.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm billing preference (publisher vs marketplace) and the billing entity name/contact.
- We (Redwood) return an accepted PO template with minimum commercial redlines called out.
- Jonas will review any legal redlines you send; if acceptable we can sign and push the publisher onboarding in parallel.

Attachments: Redwood_Commercial_Summary_v2.xlsx; Azure_PrivateCatalog_Governance_Checklist.pdf (stubs).

Best,
Olga Petrov

Thanks Olga / team. Vendor ops reviewed and attached a completed PO with our standard commercial redlines — see Lumen_PO_signed_redlines.pdf (stub).

Two clarifications we flagged:
- Section 4 (Data residency): we need the agreement to reflect that LumenHealth customer data remains within the US region when processed via Redwood in the private catalog context. Can you confirm where runtime will be hosted and whether that can be contractually guaranteed?
- Invoicing cadence: procurement prefers Azure-billed if it simplifies our internal cost allocation, but they also noted Azure may not support some publisher-level credits we planned for. Can Redwood advise if there is any difference in discounts/credits between publisher-billed vs marketplace-billed purchases?

Evelyn / Procurement team — thanks for the redlines and the clear questions. I reviewed Lumen_PO_signed_redlines.pdf and summarized our position below.

Summary of legal response (high level):
- Data residency: Redwood can commit to US-only runtime for the LumenHealth private catalog SKU. We'll include a Data Residency addendum referencing the Azure region(s) and the operational controls.
- Indemnity/limitation: small adjustments requested to align to our standard publisher terms; we accept the commercial caps as proposed but request a carve-out for third-party cloud provider obligations — suggested language attached (redlines_jonas_comments.pdf).
- Payment / invoicing: both publisher-billed and marketplace-billed are acceptable. Note: credits applied at publisher-level (e.g., customer-specific discounts or promotional credits we provide) are typically easier to track with publisher-billed invoices. Marketplace-billed purchases route through Azure and can limit the application of publisher-originated credits. Finance (cc'd Rishi) can provide detailed guidance on incentives.

Next steps:
1) Rishi will follow up with the finance note on credit differences and invoice samples.
2) If Lumen confirms marketplace vs publisher billing preference we will finalize the PO and push the DocuSign package.
3) Olga / Marissa will initiate Azure publisher onboarding (seller auth + tenant linking) after the executed PO.

Attaching: redlines_jonas_comments.pdf (legal redline suggestions).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
